subject: rider
name: Safe Handling & Restraint
summary: Approaching, moving around, reading basic body language, and tying or restraining a horse safely.
purpose: Prevents preventable injuries to both horse and handler during everyday care and preparation.
safety: Always announce your presence before approaching blind spots.
Avoid standing directly behind the hindquarters or wrapping lead ropes around hands or body.
Use a safe tie point at or above wither height with an emergency release method.

introductory.overview: Safe positioning around a calm, cooperative horse and basic safe tying.

components.title: Approaching and moving around
components.description: Approaching at the shoulder, staying close or well clear when passing behind, and keeping exits unblocked.

components.title: Safe tying
components.description: Choosing a solid tie point, adjusting rope length safely, and using a quick-release knot or breakaway arrangement.

introductory.learning: Approaches and ties a quiet horse with reminders about blind spots, rope handling, or tie length.
introductory.proficient: Independently approaches, moves around, and ties a cooperative horse safely, maintaining safe positioning, rope management, and emergency release readiness.

intermediate.overview: Adapting handling and restraint thoughtfully for anxious, green, or unfamiliar horses and varied environments.

components.title: Reading early tension
components.description: Recognizing ear, eye, posture, and breathing cues before a horse reacts.

components.title: Choosing restraint
components.description: Deciding when to tie, cross-tie, or have a handler hold the horse based on the situation.

intermediate.learning: Adjusts handling for mild tension or busy environments with occasional coaching.
intermediate.proficient: Independently reads early signs of discomfort, selects appropriate restraint or holding methods for the setting, and keeps both horse and bystanders safe.

subject: rider
name: Grooming
summary: Keeping a horse's coat, skin, mane, tail, and hooves clean and healthy while noticing changes in condition.
purpose: Supports equine comfort and hygiene, builds handling confidence, and serves as the primary daily check for injuries or abnormalities.
safety: Work from safe positions and watch the horse's body language.
Take care around sensitive areas, slippery wash areas, chilling after bathing, and product sensitivities.

introductory.overview: Routine full-body grooming, hoof cleaning, and noticing obvious abnormalities on a cooperative horse.

components.title: Routine coat, mane, and tail care
components.description: Using appropriate brushes gently and effectively without pulling hair or irritating sensitive areas.

components.title: Hoof picking
components.description: Safely asking for and cleaning all four hooves, checking for thrush, packed debris, or loose shoes.

components.title: Tool hygiene and obvious checks
components.description: Cleaning tools and spotting obvious cuts, heat, swelling, or missing shoes.

introductory.learning: Grooms and cleans hooves on a cooperative horse with guidance or occasional reminders about positioning or thoroughness.
introductory.proficient: Independently and safely grooms a cooperative horse thoroughly, cleans all four hooves, maintains safe positioning, and notices and reports obvious problems.

intermediate.overview: Bathing, seasonal coat management, adapting to individual sensitivities, and spotting subtle abnormalities.

components.title: Bathing and drying
components.description: Safe water introduction, thorough rinsing, scraping, and weather-appropriate drying.

components.title: Seasonal coat care
components.description: Managing heavy shedding, winter coats, mud, and rain-related skin issues.

components.title: Subtle condition checks
components.description: Recognizing early skin conditions, mild filling or heat, hoof changes, and body-condition shifts.

intermediate.learning: Bathes and manages seasonal care with guidance; beginning to spot subtle changes but seeks confirmation.
intermediate.proficient: Independently plans and carries out grooming suited to season, weather, and horse sensitivity—including safe bathing—and knows when to monitor, adjust care, or seek advice.

subject: rider
name: Blanketing
summary: Selecting, fitting, putting on, and removing horse blankets or sheets safely across different designs.
purpose: Protects horses from weather when needed while preventing rubbing, overheating, or dangerous strap entanglement.
safety: Fasten chest straps first when putting on and unfasten them last when removing.
Never leave leg straps or belly surcingles dangling where a horse could catch a hoof.

introductory.overview: Safely putting on, adjusting, and removing a properly sized blanket on a cooperative horse.

components.title: Safe sequence
components.description: Folding cleanly onto the back, fastening front-to-back, and unfastening back-to-front.

components.title: Strap adjustment
components.description: Securing belly and leg straps without twisting or excessive slack.

introductory.learning: Puts on and removes a blanket with reminders on strap order or adjustment.
introductory.proficient: Independently puts on, adjusts, and removes different blanket designs safely without startling the horse or leaving straps loose.

intermediate.overview: Evaluating blanket fit, weight selection for weather and coat, and checking for rubs or overheating.

components.title: Weight and weather judgment
components.description: Choosing appropriate turnout, stable, or cooler weights based on clipping, shelter, and forecast.

components.title: Fit and pressure checks
components.description: Checking wither clearance, shoulder freedom, and early rub marks.

intermediate.learning: Selects blanket weights and checks fit with occasional guidance.
intermediate.proficient: Independently selects appropriate blankets for conditions, evaluates fit across movement, and identifies and corrects rubbing or overheating early.

subject: rider
name: Health Monitoring
summary: Assessing a horse's daily appearance, demeanor, and vital signs to establish baselines and spot illness or injury early.
purpose: Early recognition of colic, fever, lameness, or infection improves treatment outcomes and welfare.
safety: Maintain safe positioning when checking temperature, digital pulses, or gut sounds.
Use clean equipment and sanitize thermometers between horses.

introductory.overview: Conducting a visual head-to-tail daily check and recognizing clear red flags.

components.title: Daily visual and physical check
components.description: Checking attitude, appetite, manure/urine, eyes, nostrils, coat, legs, and hooves.

components.title: Red flags
components.description: Recognizing acute colic signs, non-weight-bearing lameness, significant swelling, or bleeding.

introductory.learning: Performs a basic health check with guidance on what is normal versus concerning.
introductory.proficient: Independently performs a systematic daily health check and promptly reports abnormal demeanor, appetite, or visible injury.

intermediate.overview: Measuring vital signs accurately, knowing normal equine ranges, and communicating findings clearly to a veterinarian.

components.title: TPR and mucous membranes
components.description: Taking rectal temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, capillary refill time, gum color, and gut sounds.

components.title: Digital pulses
components.description: Palpating digital pulses and noting abnormal warmth in the hoof.

intermediate.learning: Measures vital signs with assistance or needs reference ranges to interpret results.
intermediate.proficient: Independently and accurately measures temperature, pulse, respiration, mucous membranes, and gut sounds, compares against normal ranges, and communicates findings clearly.

subject: rider
name: First Aid
summary: Providing safe initial care for minor wounds and stabilizing common equine emergencies while awaiting veterinary guidance.
purpose: Prevents contamination or worsening of injuries and keeps the horse calm and safe until a veterinarian arrives.
safety: Prioritize human safety when a horse is painful or panicked.
Do not apply unapproved topical products to deep wounds before veterinary evaluation.

intermediate.overview: Maintaining a barn first-aid kit, cleaning minor superficial wounds, and managing emergencies calmly.

components.title: Minor wound care
components.description: Rinsing, assessing location (especially near joints/tendons), and applying appropriate basic dressings.

components.title: Emergency triage
components.description: Controlling bleeding with clean pressure, keeping a colicking or injured horse safe, and contacting a vet promptly.

intermediate.learning: Assists with basic wound cleaning and kit use under supervision.
intermediate.proficient: Independently assesses minor wounds, performs safe initial cleaning/protection, recognizes injuries requiring immediate veterinary care, and stabilizes emergencies calmly.

subject: rider
name: Administering Medications
summary: Safely preparing and administering prescribed or approved oral medications according to veterinary or label instructions.
purpose: Ensures horses receive accurate doses calmly without stress, aspiration, or wasted medication.
safety: Verify the right horse, medication, dose, and route every time.
Ensure the horse's mouth is empty of hay/grain before using an oral syringe.

intermediate.overview: Accurate dosing and calm administration via oral syringe, top-dressing, or other approved oral methods.

components.title: Verification and dosing
components.description: Reading labels, measuring doses accurately, and logging administration.

components.title: Calm delivery
components.description: Administering via feed or oral syringe without fighting the horse's head.

intermediate.learning: Measures and administers oral medication with supervision or reminders.
intermediate.proficient: Independently verifies instructions, measures accurate doses, administers oral medications calmly and safely, and confirms the full dose is taken.

subject: rider
name: Leg Wraps & Bandaging
summary: Selecting, applying, inspecting, and removing standing wraps, exercise wraps, or basic medical bandages safely.
purpose: Protects lower limbs during travel, rest, exercise, or wound care without causing tendon pressure or circulation issues.
safety: Apply even tension without wrinkles or ridges over tendons.
Avoid kneeling on both knees beside the horse; stay ready to step away.

intermediate.overview: Applying appropriate padding and wraps with safe, even tension and recognizing complications.

components.title: Wrap selection and padding
components.description: Matching wrap type (standing, exercise, medical) and padding to the purpose.

components.title: Even tension and inspection
components.description: Wrapping smoothly around the cannon bone and checking for heat, swelling, or slipped wraps.

intermediate.learning: Applies leg wraps with guidance to correct tension, overlap, or padding alignment.
intermediate.proficient: Independently selects, applies, inspects, and removes standing, exercise, or basic medical wraps with even tension, smooth padding, and awareness of complications.

subject: rider
name: Feeding
summary: Following feeding routines safely, checking feed and water quality, and understanding core equine nutritional principles.
purpose: Supports digestive health and reduces the risk of colic, choke, or barn-aisle conflict during feeding time.
safety: Keep feed rooms securely latched.
Follow safe feeding order in group or barn settings to prevent kicking or biting over food.

introductory.overview: Measuring and delivering established rations safely while checking forage and water quality.

components.title: Ration delivery
components.description: Following feed charts by weight/scoop accurately and delivering safely.

components.title: Quality checks
components.description: Checking water cleanliness and inspecting hay and grain for mold, dust, or foreign objects.

introductory.learning: Delivers feed and checks water with supervision or feed-chart reminders.
introductory.proficient: Independently follows feeding schedules accurately, maintains clean water, inspects feed quality, and feeds safely without rushing or causing agitation.

intermediate.overview: Adjusting feeding routines thoughtfully for workload, body condition, and gradual diet transitions.

components.title: Forage-first principles
components.description: Understanding why forage is the foundation, small frequent meals, and gradual transitions.

components.title: Condition and workload
components.description: Recognizing weight loss/gain trends and knowing when to consult an owner, trainer, or vet.

intermediate.learning: Discusses diet adjustments and body condition with guidance.
intermediate.proficient: Independently evaluates forage quality, water intake, and body condition, plans safe gradual feed transitions, and spots feeding-related risks early.

subject: rider
name: Stable Care
summary: Maintaining clean, dry, hazard-free stalls, shelters, and turnout areas.
purpose: Protects respiratory and hoof health while preventing injuries from sharp hardware, toxic plants, or damaged fencing.
safety: Keep pitchforks and wheelbarrows positioned safely away from horses.
Do not leave stall doors unlatched or tools in walkways.

introductory.overview: Thorough stall/shelter cleaning, safe tool handling, and daily hazard checks.

components.title: Cleaning and bedding
components.description: Removing manure and wet bedding, banking or leveling clean bedding, and scrubbing water buckets.

components.title: Hazard checks
components.description: Checking latches, protruding nails, fencing, and toxic weeds.

introductory.learning: Cleans stalls and checks water with reminders on thoroughness or tool placement.
introductory.proficient: Independently cleans and beds stalls or shelters thoroughly, handles tools safely around horses, and identifies and reports physical hazards.

subject: rider
name: Tack Use, Fit & Care
summary: Putting on, adjusting, safety-checking, removing, and maintaining saddles, bridles, halters, and protective gear.
purpose: Ensures equipment is comfortable for the horse, secure for the rider, and free from worn stitching or unsafe fit.
safety: Inspect stitching, billets, girth buckles, and reins before every ride.
Check girth tightness gradually and re-check before mounting.

introductory.overview: Tacking up, untacking, performing pre-ride safety checks, and routine cleaning on familiar tack.

components.title: Tacking up and untacking
components.description: Calmly placing pad/saddle and bridle or halter without bumping teeth, ears, or back; removing and storing neatly.

components.title: Safety and basic fit check
components.description: Checking wither clearance, girth alignment, bit/headstall placement, and worn leather or hardware.

components.title: Routine tack care
components.description: Wiping down sweat and dirt after rides and conditioning leather or washing synthetic gear appropriately.

introductory.learning: Tacks up, checks fit, and cleans gear with occasional supervision or reminders.
introductory.proficient: Independently and calmly tacks up and untacks a cooperative horse, completes a thorough pre-ride safety and basic fit check, and cleans and stores equipment properly.

intermediate.overview: Evaluating saddle and bridle fit across conformation and movement, and adapting equipment thoughtfully.

components.title: Functional fit assessment
components.description: Assessing saddle balance, gullet/shoulder clearance, pad bulk, and bridle/bit comfort.

components.title: Deep maintenance
components.description: Disassembling, inspecting hidden wear points, conditioning, and knowing when repair or professional saddle fitting is needed.

intermediate.learning: Evaluates fit and wear patterns with guidance.
intermediate.proficient: Independently assesses saddle, pad, and bridle fit statically and in motion, recognizes signs of tack discomfort or unsafe wear, and adjusts or seeks qualified fitting appropriately.
